meeting_header: Recorded: 2026-05-09 14:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Location: Zoom | Recording: available | Attendees: Aisha Khan (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Lighthouse Head of MLOps), Sofia Jensen (Engineering Manager), Tom Reynolds (Procurement)
summary: Lighthouse Financial is aiming to increase their committed retainer (~2x) to support growth and activate an EU serving region within Q3. The call covered tradeoffs between Reserved (Dedicated) capacity vs Hosted with burst, EU Private deployment considerations for data residency, and security artifacts (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs). Redwood will provide revised pricing and run a technical benchmark using Lighthouse sample prompts. Agreement to draft amendment and target to finalize commercial terms by late May.
topics: Capacity uplift options (reserved vs hosted + burst)
EU region onboarding and private/VPC options
Security/compliance: SOC 2, KMS, audit logs, SSO
Benchmark plan: latency, throughput, cost per token
transcript:
Meeting start header: 2026-05-09 14:00 UTC — duration ~48m.

[00:00] Aisha Khan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Aisha from Redwood — joining with Miguel on the deep tech bits. How are we all?
[00:06] Raj Patel: Good, thanks. Quick note, we're juggling Q3 launch windows so want to nail timeline today.
[00:12] Sofia Jensen: Yeah hi, Sofia here, we'll cover engineering constraints.
[00:15] Tom Reynolds: Tom from procurement, I'll be focusing on contract and timelines.
[00:20] Aisha Khan: Awesome. Brief agenda: we want to run through capacity uplift, EU region activation, security checks, and get to next steps on pricing and amendment. Sound right?
[00:30] Raj Patel: Yes, specifically we need predictable p95 latency for chat and a cost envelope. We may double our current commitment if numbers line up.
[00:40] Miguel Santos: Cool, I'll jump into numbers later. To frame options: Reserved/Dedicated capacity gives the most predictable throughput and lower p95, Hosted with burst is cheaper up front but can have slightly higher tail latency depending on burst load. Also KV cache behavior and batching matter a lot for cost.
[00:55] Sofia Jensen: On the private side, data residency is a showstopper — EU data at rest and key management inside our KMS is required. Do you support customer-managed keys?
[01:05] Miguel Santos: Yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations in Private deployments; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key for certain tiers. There was a note about an earlier product name, Redwood Privatee — apologies, that was our internal shorthand.
[01:18] Raj Patel: Right. The other thing is our prompt lengths vary: p50 token is ~180, p95 ~1,100 tokens, and concurrency spikes around 250 concurrent calls during market open.
[01:30] Miguel Santos: That's helpful. With those numbers, Reserved Dedicated pools look better for keeping stable p95 under 250 concurrency. We can do autoscaling but warm pools reduce cold-start impact. Also prefix cache (we saw 'KV cash' in a previous doc) — prefix/KV caching can cut downstream token spend significantly for repeated context.
[01:48] Sofia Jensen: If we go Dedicated, how fast can you provision EU nodes? We need EU region live before end of Q3.
[01:56] Aisha Khan: Typically EU provisioning for Dedicated is ~4–8 weeks once contracts and capacity are committed; Private onprem is longer. For a 12-month amendment we can prioritize capacity provisioning. We'll capture exact SLA and lead times in the amendment.
[02:12] Tom Reynolds: Procurement question — we need to see SOC 2 type ii and ISO docs, plus a network diagram showing VPC peering. Can you share those?
[02:20] Miguel Santos: Absolutely. We'll share SOC 2 and ISO attestations and a standard VPC architecture diagram. Note that audit logs and per-token tracing live in Redwood Console; we can give a screenshot but full access requires an environment.
[02:33] Raj Patel: Also, for costs: show us committed cost per token and then burst surcharge. We want transparency: cost per generation token vs embeddings.
[02:42] Aisha Khan: Understood. We'll prepare a revised pricing sheet that shows committed tiers, burst rates, and a worked example for your typical monthly traffic.
[02:50] Sofia Jensen: For technical vetting, we'd like to run a benchmark: our top-10 prompts, real concurrency, and a few models you recommend. Can Miguel run that with us?
[02:58] Miguel Santos: Yes, we prefer to run it together remotely. We'll do Dedicated vs Hosted runs and report latency (p50/p95), throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also test quantized variants if you want to trade accuracy for cost.
[03:12] Raj Patel: Quantization ok as long as evaluations don't regress. We need to keep output quality. Do you link regressions to your Optimize tooling?
[03:20] Miguel Santos: We have Redwood Optimize suggestions and quality monitoring tied to prompt sets/evals. We can run regression alerts against your reference prompts.
[03:28] Tom Reynolds: Cool. Timeline check: procurement wants an amendment by mid-May to meet internal approval cycles. Is that feasible?
[03:36] Aisha Khan: We'll aim to deliver a draft amendment plus pricing by 2026-05-12. That gives you a week to run internal review before procurement signatures.
[03:45] Sofia Jensen: Technical deep-dive: Miguel, can you clarify how failover works across regions? If EU goes down, do we have automatic fallback to US? What's the data path?
[03:55] Miguel Santos: We have smart routing policies — you can route by latency, cost, region, or tier. For EU-first customers we recommend local primary serving with fallback to a non-EU replica if allowed. Note this has data residency implications; fallback may not be allowed for regulated data. We'll document options.
[04:12] Raj Patel: We won't allow regulated PII to leave EU. Some non-PII workloads can fail over.
[04:18] Miguel Santos: Ok, we'll make that explicit in the design doc.
[04:22] Sofia Jensen: Any notes about profiling? We saw a weird spike earlier where p99 jumped during batch windows. Is continuous batching something you tune per workload?
[04:32] Miguel Santos: Yes, continuous batching parameters, kernel selection, and batch size are tuned to workload. For chat you generally want smaller batches to reduce latency, for batch embedding workloads you optimize for throughput. We'll run the test plan to surface tuning knobs.
[04:44] Aisha Khan: Competitor aside, do you have any blockers leaning you away from Redwood?
[04:48] Raj Patel: Main concerns are vendor lock and the unknowns around cost at sustained higher volume. Also, we want to confirm the SLA for p95 latency in the amendment.
[04:58] Aisha Khan: Great feedback — we'll be explicit on SLA and include cost sensitivity scenarios. We'll also include an escape clause for scale-related regressions in the amendment.
[05:06] Tom Reynolds: On legal side, we need a redlineable amendment and an outline of liability and data handling.
[05:12] Aisha Khan: We'll push the amendment and legal appendix for your review.
[05:15] Sofia Jensen: Can we also request a short run-book for on-call and incident escalations? We want to know points of contact and MTTR targets.
[05:22] Miguel Santos: Yes, we'll provide an on-call playbook excerpt and typical escalation matrix.
[05:28] Raj Patel: For the benchmark, can you include a test that simulates our worst-case market open spike? That'll validate autoscaling and warm pool performance.
[05:36] Miguel Santos: We'll do a spike test with 250–300 concurrent streams and warm pools pre-warming, and compare Dedicated vs Hosted behavior.
[05:44] Sofia Jensen: Also, what observability will we get? Token-level breakdown, per-route dashboards?
[05:50] Miguel Santos: Console provides per-route/model dashboards, traces, and token-level cost breakdowns. Retention can be an add-on if you want longer history.
[06:00] Tom Reynolds: For procurement, can you list billing cadence and invoicing terms? Net 30? Net 60?
[06:08] Aisha Khan: Standard is Net 30 but we can discuss Net 45/60 for larger deals. We'll include proposed terms in the amendment.
[06:16] Raj Patel: One more technical: does Redwood support function/tool calling or structured outputs for our downstream systems?
[06:24] Miguel Santos: Yes, streaming, function calling, and structured output are supported in the API. We'll include sample payloads.
[06:30] Sofia Jensen: About private on-prem path — if we later want to move to onprem, are there migration tools?
[06:36] Miguel Santos: We have deployment abstractions and migration guidance; moving from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private has steps and lead times, we'll outline them.
[06:44] Aisha Khan: Ok to recap: Redwood sends revised pricing and amendment draft by 2026-05-12; security docs and network diagram; Miguel runs benchmark week of 5/18 with Lighthouse prompts; Lighthouse provides sample traffic and prompt set. Procurement will review amendment and revert. Any additions?
[06:58] Raj Patel: Please call out p95 SLA target and warm pool lead times in the amendment.
[07:04] Tom Reynolds: And attach invoice terms and contact for billing.
[07:08] Aisha Khan: Noted. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in an email with links to the shared spreadsheet and calendar invite for the benchmark.
[07:16] Sofia Jensen: Thanks, talk soon.
[07:18] Raj Patel: Thanks.
[07:20] Meeting end.

Notes: transcription has a few mis-heard product names (e.g., Redwood Privatee; KV cash) and filler words. References to shared artifacts: pricing sheet (link to be shared), security pack (SOC 2/ISO), benchmark spreadsheet (to be uploaded to shared drive).
